thread:
anna: Quick perf heads-up — after flipping remat=layer on the 70B config (tp=4 pp=2) we see ~9% median token-latency regression on our 8xA100 gates. root run: https://console.redwood/perf/70b/remat-run-1802506789
raj: ok can you paste the top-level profiler summary or a flame trace?
anna: uploaded trace to s3: s3://redwood-perf/70b/remat/1802506789/trace.json. Top-line from perf sampler: 
```
wait_for_allreduce: 42% (was 18%)
recompute_kernels: 28%
kv_cache_accesses: 12% (miss rate +7pp)
```
mikhail: remat increases recompute compute, but why does allreduce jump that much? sounds like worse overlap/queueing.
lisa: my guess — recompute changes execution order so backward work doesn't overlap with the all-reduce windows, forcing global syncs to block. also KV warmup order could be breaking cache locality.
raj: please run toggles: async_allreduce true/false; kv cache warmup on/off; kernel selector diagnostics. also add TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=INFO for collect.
anna: running now. command used: 
```
./run_infer --model redwood-70b --tp 4 --pp 2 --remat layer --trace perf.json --async_allreduce true --kv_warmup on
```
anna: quick results: async_allreduce=true => 8.9% regression; async_allreduce=false => 4.1% regression. So async helps but doesn't restore baseline.
mikhail: interesting. what did kernel selector say? any fallbacks for recompute kernels?
anna: yes — selector logged fallback on a few recompute layers due to mixed-precision path mismatch: 
```
kernel_selector: layer_102 fallback matmul_fast->matmul_generic
kernel_selector: layer_137 fallback fused_attn->attn_generic
```
raj: those fallbacks could lengthen recompute stages and widen the window where allreduce enqueues. could also increase temp memory pressure and change cache eviction timing. try forcing the fast kernels for recompute path (force_kernel_route=prefer_fast) and run again. watch for numerical diffs.
lisa: also test remat granularity: layer vs block vs none. smaller remat blocks might reduce per-recompute latency and let overlap improve.
anna: did a quick test: turned off remat for KV-eligible layers (so we don't rebuild KVs in a different order) and regression dropped to 1.5%. So KV ordering looks relevant.
raj: that aligns — if remat causes KV writes/reads to happen earlier/later on different ranks, you can get more misses and extra data movement that hurts allreduce concurrency.
mikhail: let's enumerate experiments to run systematically: 
- sweep remat granularity: none / layer / block (block=8 layers)
- kernel route: prefer_fast / prefer_stable / allow_fallbacks
- async_allreduce on/off
- kv_pin: enabled/disabled (pin hot prefixes during recompute)
- micro-batcher sizes [1,2,4,8] to see amortization effects
We should collect compute_overlap_ratio, allreduce_queue_size, kv_miss_rate per-step.
anna: added compute_overlap extractor to perf tools. one-liner to get metric: 
```
python tools/compute_overlap.py perf.json --metric compute_overlap_ratio
```
anna: initial micro-batcher note: larger micro-batches amortize allreduce frequency so latency reg shrinks but tail per-token latency rises. need to find sweet spot for production.
raj: also check NCCL tuning parameters: NCCL_NSOCKS_PERTHREAD, NCCL_BUFFSIZE — small buffers + many sockets can increase op fragmentation. Could be amplified by recompute bursts.
lisa: good point. We should try bumping NCCL_BUFFSIZE and toggling NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE to see effect on short allreduces during recompute.
anna: quick numbers from the first mini-sweep (tp2 pp2 on 2xA100 as cheap proxy): 
- baseline (no remat): median token latency 12.3ms
- remat=layer: 13.7ms (+11.4%)
- remat=block(8): 12.9ms (+4.9%)
- remat=layer + force_fast_kernels: 12.6ms (+2.4%)
- remat=layer + kv_pin: 12.4ms (+0.8%)
So block remat + kernel route + kv pin looks promising.
mikhail: nice — that suggests we can mitigate most of the regression via config levers without changing algorithm. For long term we should patch kernel selector to prefer fused kernels for recompute paths and make KV pinning automatic when remat is enabled.
raj: I'll open a ticket to codify the sweep and track perf numbers across tp/pp shapes. also add a regression guard in CI for 70B with remat enabled.
infra-bot: created PERF-2386: "Remat-induced allreduce amplification on 70B (tp4 pp2)" https://issues.redwood/PERF-2386
perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/infer/70b/remat/1802506789 (summary & traces)
lisa: small design thought — we could try speculative allreduce kickoff during recompute when partial KV outputs are stable. Might hide collective latency. Need to be careful about overlapping writes.
mikhail: agree, but start with safe config fixes. kernel selector change + kv pinning + micro-batch recommendation could be low-risk.
anna: next steps: schedule full sweep on tp4pp2 tonight, collect overlap metric, kernel logs, and kv stats, then post numbers here. I'll also prototype forcing fused kernels for recompute in a branch.
raj: thanks anna. create a short doc with recommended production knobs for remat if you can. cc eng-runtime-kernels and eng-runtime-kv.
anna: will do. I'll post the doc and link the ticket.
:thumbsup: reactions
